newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle sales moderate at $64 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle sales moderate at $64 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. central and southern Plains feedlot cattle sold at $64.00 per cwt in light to moderate activity, unchanged from thin activity on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
Between 8,000 and 10,000 head sold in Texas and about 10,000 in Kansas, although numbers could climb as more sales are tallied, they said.
But most owners passed bids of $63.00 and $64.00 and still were pricing cattle at $65.00.
"There's a feeling among those selling at $64.00 that beef demand could slow down after this week," a Kansas source said.
Fed cattle prices this week at $64.00 were up $1.00 from last week and supported by sharply higher beef prices.
Beef values jumped on tight inventories and demand from retailers booking for beef promotions at the end of the month and for the Independence Day holiday, market sources said.
"Probably after this week, most of the Fourth of July business will have been taken care of," a Kansas source said.
Those holding out for $65.00 regarded Wednesday's sales as "hand-to-mouth" by packers and suggested they were still short on inventory, several cattle feeders said.
"If they still need cattle, we can get the $65.00," a western Oklahoma source said.
